name: Green tea
description: Unoxidized tea — the cooling end of the tea spectrum.

tcm.note: Clears heat; the summer tea.

ayurveda.note: Astringent-bitter; light.

histamine.note: Tea inhibits DAO — a consideration when flaring, fine otherwise.

name: Black tea
description: Fully oxidized tea — the base of desi chai and Arab shai.

tcm.note: Oxidation warms it: hong cha is the winter tea.

unani.note: Chai is treated as garam in desi usage.

histamine.note: Same DAO note as green tea.

name: Masala chai
description: Black tea boiled with milk, ginger, and warming spices.

tcm.note: Warming tea + warming spices.

unani.note: The default garam drink of the subcontinent.

histamine.note: Tea's DAO note; spices mostly benign.

name: Coffee
description: Roasted bean brew, espresso to qahwa.

tcm.note: Bitter-warming, drying.

ayurveda.note: Rajasic stimulant.

histamine.note: Caffeine blocks DAO and can trigger the sensitive — a common flare culprit.

name: Chrysanthemum tea
description: Sweet floral infusion — TCM's go-to heat clearer.

tcm.note: Classic for 'heatiness': red eyes, sore throat.

ayurveda.note: Not classical; inferred.

histamine.note: Caffeine-free; gentle.

name: Mint tea
description: Fresh mint steeped alone (Maghrebi style adds green tea).

histamine.note: One of the safest hot drinks when reactive.

name: Hibiscus (karkade)
description: Ruby-red tart infusion, iced in Egyptian summers.

ayurveda.note: Sour yet classed cooling — an exception like amla.

unani.note: Served as a summer cooler across the Arab world.

histamine.note: Well tolerated; sparse formal data.

name: Lemonade / shikanjvi
description: Lemon, water, sugar — the subcontinent's first response to heat.

ayurveda.note: Sour is heating on paper, yet nimbu pani is universally used as a cooler.

unani.note: Shikanjabeen descends from classical Unani sikanjabin.

histamine.note: Citrus liberator note — skip when flaring, fine for heat.

name: Sugarcane juice
description: Fresh-pressed cane — the streetside summer glass.

tcm.note: Sugarcane clears heat and moistens in TCM.

histamine.note: Fresh-pressed is fine; hygiene of the press matters more.

name: Coconut water
description: The young coconut's electrolyte water.

ayurveda.note: The classic pitta emergency drink.

histamine.note: Excellent when reactive AND overheated.

name: Lassi (sweet)
description: Churned yogurt whipped with water and sugar.

tcm.note: Not classical.

ayurveda.note: Churning + dilution tempers dahi's heat, say the texts — sweet lassi lands cooling-ish.

histamine.note: As yogurt.

name: Rose sharbat (Rooh Afza)
description: The crimson rose syrup of Ramadan tables and loo summers.

tcm.note: Not classical; rose itself is mildly cool-moving.

ayurveda.note: Rose is a classic pitta cooler.

unani.note: Rooh Afza was formulated BY a Unani hakim as a heat remedy.

histamine.note: Syrup base benign; check bottle additives if very sensitive.

name: Orange juice
description: The breakfast juice.

ayurveda.note: Follows orange's sour-heating read.

histamine.note: Concentrated citrus — a notable liberator serving.

name: Cola / soda
description: Carbonated sweet caffeine.

tcm.note: Served iced = cold-damp burden in TCM's view; the drink itself isn't classical.

ayurveda.note: Stimulant-sweet; not classical.

histamine.note: Caffeine's DAO note; additives vary by brand.

name: Barley water (jau/talbina)
description: Strained barley infusion — a cooler in three traditions at once.

unani.note: Ma' al-sha'ir is a canonical Unani cooling prescription.

histamine.note: Very gentle — good reactive-day drink.

name: Sattu sharbat
description: Roasted gram flour whisked in water — Bihar's field-day cooler.

tcm.note: Not classical.

ayurveda.note: Famous summer cooling drink despite chana's warm lean — roasting + dilution.

histamine.note: Gentle; sparse formal data.

name: Soy milk
description: The Chinese breakfast milk.

tcm.note: Fresh dou jiang neutral-cool, moistening.

ayurveda.note: Not classical.

histamine.note: Soy's modest flag; fine for many.

name: Almond milk
description: Nut milk — modern carton or classical badam sardai.

tcm.note: Not classical.

ayurveda.note: Soaked-peeled almonds ground in milk/water = the cooling sardai logic.

unani.note: Sardai is served as a cooler despite badam being garam — processing flips it.

histamine.note: As almonds, diluted.

name: Oat milk
description: Creamy grain milk of coffee shops.

tcm.note: Not classical; follows oats' warm lean, diluted.

ayurveda.note: Follows oats, mildly.

histamine.note: Well tolerated.

name: Kombucha
description: Fermented sweet tea — trendy, and a histamine triple-hit.

tcm.note: Thinly classified.

ayurveda.note: Sour-fermented = ushna.

histamine.note: Fermented + tea + acids: among the worst drinks for histamine intolerance.

name: Oolong tea
description: Half-oxidised leaf, somewhere between green and black in both colour and character.

tcm.note: Sits between green (cool) and black (warm) precisely because it is half-oxidised — the moderate everyday tea.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry; caffeine reads as ushna.

histamine.note: Lower than black tea, higher than green — oxidation is the variable.

name: White tea
description: The youngest buds, barely processed — pale and delicate.

tcm.note: The least processed and coolest of the teas; taken in summer to clear heat.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry; read from its minimal processing.

histamine.note: Low; the least processed tea.

name: Pu-erh tea
description: Tea deliberately aged and fermented for years — earthy and dark.

tcm.note: The ripened kind is warm and famously taken after fatty meals to move stagnation.

ayurveda.note: Fermented and caffeinated, so ushna.

histamine.note: Years of deliberate microbial fermentation — the highest of the teas by a distance.

name: Jasmine tea
description: Green tea scented by layering it with fresh jasmine blossom.

tcm.note: Follows green tea; the jasmine adds a gentle qi-moving, mood-easing quality.

ayurveda.note: Read with green tea.

histamine.note: Low, as green tea is.

name: Chamomile tea
description: Dried daisy flowers steeped for a soft, apple-scented calm.

tcm.note: Read with the chrysanthemum family — cooling and heat-clearing.

ayurveda.note: Shita and calming to pitta.

unani.note: Babunaj is classed garam in the Unani record, given to relax spasms and disperse wind — the reverse of the Chinese reading.

histamine.note: Low. It is in the ragweed family, which matters for pollen allergy rather than histamine.

name: Ginger tea
description: Fresh ginger simmered in water — the first thing made at the first sign of a chill.

tcm.note: Sheng jiang releases the exterior and warms the middle — the classic first-day-of-a-cold drink.

ayurveda.note: Ardraka is ushna and deepana, the universal digestive kindler.

unani.note: Zanjabeel is garam-khushk in a high degree.

histamine.note: Very low — one of the safest hot drinks on a reactive day.

name: Fennel tea
description: Fennel seed steeped in hot water — drunk after heavy meals, and given to babies for colic.

tcm.note: Xiao hui xiang is warm and disperses cold from the lower abdomen.

ayurveda.note: Saunf is classically shita and pitta-pacifying — the reason it is chewed after a meal.

unani.note: Thanda in desi usage, taken against acidity — the opposite of the Chinese reading.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Jeera water
description: Cumin seed boiled in water and cooled — the everyday digestive glass.

tcm.note: Cumin is warm and moves the middle burner.

ayurveda.note: Jiraka is ushna and deepana-pachana — kindling for a dull digestion.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Thandai
description: Milk ground with almonds, melon seeds, fennel and pepper — the Holi cooler.

tcm.note: Read from its components; the melon seeds and milk dominate.

ayurveda.note: Built deliberately from shita dravyas — milk, char magaz, saunf and rose.

unani.note: Thanda-tar by design; the name is literally 'the cooling one'.

histamine.note: Almonds and milk are low; it is the nut-heavy base that keeps it modest rather than zero.

name: Jaljeera
description: Sharp, salty, minty cumin water — sold ice-cold from street carts.

tcm.note: The mint and tamarind pull cool against the cumin's warmth.

ayurveda.note: Mint and amchur make it shita overall, despite the heating jeera.

unani.note: Served as a thanda drink against summer heat and poor appetite.

histamine.note: Amchur and tamarind base — sour and concentrated.

name: Aam panna
description: Roasted green mango pulp with cumin, mint and salt — the drink given against heatstroke.

tcm.note: Sour unripe fruit; no classical entry.

ayurveda.note: Unripe mango is amla-rasa and ushna in the classical reading, whatever the drink is used for.

unani.note: The standard desi drink against loo — thanda in practice, which is the whole point of it.

histamine.note: Green mango base, sour and concentrated.

name: Nimbu pani
description: Lemon, water, sugar and salt — the fastest thing to make in a heatwave.

tcm.note: Follows lemon, which is cool and generates fluids.

ayurveda.note: Nimbu is amla-rasa and ushna — sour is heating, however cold the glass.

unani.note: Thanda in desi usage; the standard summer drink.

histamine.note: Citrus liberator.

name: Badam milk
description: Milk simmered with ground almonds, saffron and cardamom — served hot in winter.

tcm.note: Nuts and saffron over a milk base, taken hot.

ayurveda.note: Badam is ushna and building; saffron more so — this outweighs milk's shita.

unani.note: Garam-tar, a classical brain and strength tonic.

histamine.note: Low; almonds and fresh milk are both modest.

name: Kahwa
description: Kashmiri green tea with saffron, cardamom and slivered almonds.

tcm.note: A cool green-tea base carrying warm spices; the spices dominate.

ayurveda.note: Saffron, cardamom and almond are all ushna.

unani.note: Garam; a winter drink of the Kashmir valley.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Tamarind drink
description: Tamarind pulp strained, sweetened and iced — a Ramadan table fixture.

tcm.note: Follows tamarind, which is cool and generates fluids.

ayurveda.note: Amlika is amla-rasa and ushna, and classically said to aggravate pitta and rakta.

unani.note: Tamr hindi is barid in the Unani record and given specifically against bilious heat and thirst.

histamine.note: Very sour and concentrated.

name: Arabic coffee
description: Pale lightly-roasted coffee heavy with cardamom, poured from a dallah.

tcm.note: Read with coffee; the cardamom adds warmth.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna — coffee and cardamom together.

unani.note: Qahwa is garam-khushk in the Arab record; the cardamom is added expressly to temper it.

histamine.note: Coffee is a liberator on the SIGHI list, roast and origin notwithstanding.

name: Karak chai
description: Black tea boiled hard with evaporated milk, sugar and cardamom.

tcm.note: Black tea plus long boiling plus warm spice.

ayurveda.note: Ushna; the milk does not offset the tea and spice.

histamine.note: Black tea is moderate; the long boil and the tinned milk both add.

name: Coconut milk
description: Pressed from grated coconut — the body of southern curries and the base of payasam.

tcm.note: Read with coconut; not a classical Chinese entry.

ayurveda.note: Narikela is shita, guru and snigdha — cooling and heavy.

unani.note: Thanda-tar; the coastal counter to garam cooking.

histamine.note: Low fresh or tinned; it sours quickly once opened.

nutrition.highlight: the body of a southern curry

name: Apple juice
description: Pressed and usually filtered clear — the mildest of the carton juices.

tcm.note: Follows apple, which is cool and generates fluids.

ayurveda.note: Shita like the fruit.

histamine.note: Lower than citrus juice; cloudy unfiltered kinds sit a little higher.

name: Pomegranate juice
description: Deep red, tart and astringent — pressed seeds and nothing else.

tcm.note: Shi liu is warm and astringent in the Chinese reading.

ayurveda.note: Dadima is shita and tridosha-pacifying — sour yet cooling, like amla.

unani.note: Anar is firmly thanda in desi and Unani usage, given in fevers.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Mango juice
description: Thick sweet pulp thinned and sweetened — sold in cartons year-round.

tcm.note: Follows the ripe mango, which TCM reads as cool.

ayurveda.note: Ripe mango is ushna and rakta-aggravating in the classical reading — the famous split with the Chinese one.

unani.note: Aam is garam-tar in desi usage, which is why it is soaked in water before eating.

histamine.note: Low, though the sugar load in carton nectar is considerable.

name: Milkshake
description: Milk blended with ice cream and flavouring until it barely moves through a straw.

tcm.note: Iced dairy is cold and damp-forming — read with ice cream.

ayurveda.note: Shita and very guru; classically the wrong thing on a weak digestion.

histamine.note: The base is modest; chocolate and strawberry versions inherit those triggers.

name: Energy drink
description: Carbonated caffeine and sugar with added taurine and B vitamins.

tcm.note: A modern product with no classical entry; stimulant and drying, read as hot.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna by its caffeine load.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; outside the classical record entirely.

histamine.note: Caffeine is a liberator, and these carry citric acid and preservatives on top.

name: Sports drink
description: Sweetened water with added salts, meant to replace what sweating takes.

tcm.note: A modern product; sweet and fluid-generating.

ayurveda.note: Read as shita from its sugar and salt-water base.

histamine.note: Low; citric acid and colourings are the usual complaints, not histamine.

name: Beer
description: Malted grain fermented with yeast and bittered with hops.

tcm.note: Pi jiu is read as cold and damp-forming — unlike spirits, which are hot.

ayurveda.note: Sura is ushna, tikshna and specifically pitta-aggravating in the classical texts.

unani.note: Fermented drinks are garam in the Unani record, whatever their temperature in the glass.

histamine.note: Yeast-fermented and unfiltered — high in histamine and a liberator besides. Alcohol also blocks DAO, the enzyme that clears histamine, so it worsens everything eaten alongside it.

name: Red wine
description: Grapes fermented on their skins, often aged in oak for years.

tcm.note: Wine is warm and blood-moving in the Chinese reading.

ayurveda.note: Madya is ushna and tikshna in a high degree — among the most pitta-provoking substances named.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; well documented in the classical record, whatever the religious position on drinking it.

histamine.note: The textbook histamine trigger: skin-contact fermentation, ageing, sulphites, and alcohol blocking DAO all at once. Red is worse than white.

name: White wine
description: Grapes fermented without their skins — lighter, sharper, usually younger.

tcm.note: Read with wine generally — warm and moving.

ayurveda.note: Madya is ushna; the colour of the grape does not change that.

unani.note: Garam-khushk, as all fermented grape drinks are.

histamine.note: Lower than red, since it ferments off the skins — but still fermented, sulphited and DAO-blocking.

name: Spirits
description: Distilled rather than merely fermented — the concentrated end of the shelf.

tcm.note: Bai jiu is hot and strongly dispersing; distilled liquor is the hottest drink in the Chinese materia.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna in the highest degree of the madya group.

histamine.note: Distilling leaves most histamine behind, so clear spirits are lower than wine or beer — but the alcohol still blocks DAO, which is the bigger problem.

name: Cider
description: Fermented apple juice — dry to sweet, still or sparkling.

tcm.note: An apple base is cool; the ferment pulls the other way.

ayurveda.note: Madya is ushna whatever fruit it starts from.

histamine.note: Fermented and usually sulphited, with the same DAO problem as any alcohol.

name: Rice wine
description: Fermented rice — drunk warm, and splashed into half of Chinese cooking.

tcm.note: Huang jiu is warm and moves qi and blood; it is used medicinally as a carrier for herbs.

ayurveda.note: Madya is ushna.

histamine.note: Fermented, and worth flagging because it goes into so many dishes — the cooking does not remove the histamine.

name: Matcha
description: Shade-grown green tea stone-ground to powder and whisked, leaf and all.

tcm.note: Read with green tea, which is cool and clears heat — drinking the whole leaf makes it stronger, not warmer.

ayurveda.note: Shita, though the caffeine load is considerable.

histamine.note: Low, like green tea; you are consuming the entire leaf, which concentrates everything in it.

name: Barley tea
description: Roasted barley steeped into a caffeine-free amber brew, drunk hot or iced.

tcm.note: Follows barley, which is cool; roasting warms it slightly.

ayurveda.note: Shita and mutrala — the same cooling logic as barley water.

unani.note: Thanda-khushk; a classical Unani cooling drink.

histamine.note: Very low; no caffeine and no ferment.

name: Hot chocolate
description: Cocoa whisked into hot milk with sugar.

tcm.note: Read with chocolate, which is warm and stimulating, over a milk base.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the cocoa; the milk is shita but does not win.

unani.note: Garam; cocoa is garam in the Unani reading.

histamine.note: Cocoa is fermented before roasting, and is both high in histamine and a liberator — the milk does not offset it.

name: Sahlab
description: Thick milk drink set with orchid-root starch and dusted with cinnamon.

tcm.note: Warm milk with cinnamon; warming and moistening.

ayurveda.note: Ushna: the spices and the starch over a shita milk base.

unani.note: Garam-tar; a winter street drink of the Levant, held to be strengthening.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Falooda
description: Rose milk with vermicelli, basil seeds and a scoop of ice cream on top.

tcm.note: Iced dairy with rose and basil seed — cold throughout.

ayurveda.note: Shita by design: rose, sabja and milk are all cooling.

unani.note: Thanda-tar; a summer drink built to cool.

histamine.note: Low, though the ice cream and rose syrup add sugar rather than histamine.

name: Jallab
description: Date and grape molasses with rose water, poured over crushed ice and pine nuts.

tcm.note: Iced and rose-scented, over a sweet molasses base.

ayurveda.note: Dates and molasses are ushna; the rose and ice pull the other way.

unani.note: Thanda in practice — a Ramadan cooler.

histamine.note: Concentrated dried-fruit molasses, which is where the rating comes from.

name: Qamar al-din
description: Apricot leather soaked overnight into a thick sweet drink for iftar.

tcm.note: Read with dried apricot, which is warming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna; dried fruit concentrated.

histamine.note: Dried fruit concentrate, like the apricot it is made from.

name: Sol kadhi
description: Pink Konkani drink of kokum and coconut milk, drunk after a heavy meal.

tcm.note: Kokum and coconut are both cooling.

ayurveda.note: Shita by both ingredients — one of the few sour drinks that is unambiguously cooling.

unani.note: Thanda-tar; taken specifically to settle heat and heavy food.

histamine.note: Kokum is sour, so flagged, though the coconut base is gentle.

name: Neer mor
description: Thin salted buttermilk with curry leaf, ginger and asafoetida.

tcm.note: Buttermilk with warm tempering; cooling overall.

ayurveda.note: Takra is ushna in the classical reading, whatever the glass feels like.

unani.note: Thanda-tar; the standard summer drink of the south.

histamine.note: Low, like buttermilk.

name: Ragi malt
description: Finger millet flour cooked into a thin porridge-drink, sweet or salted.

tcm.note: Follows ragi, which is cooling.

ayurveda.note: Shita and building; a summer breakfast drink.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Malt drink
description: Malted barley and milk powder, whisked into hot milk.

tcm.note: A modern product; malted grain in warm milk reads as warming.

ayurveda.note: Ushna: malt and sugar over milk.

unani.note: Garam-tar; marketed and used as a strengthening drink.

histamine.note: Malt extract and milk powder, both processed and long-stored.

name: Rooibos
description: South African red bush infusion — caffeine-free, naturally sweet, no bitterness.

tcm.note: Not in the Chinese record; a mild caffeine-free infusion.

ayurveda.note: No classical entry.

histamine.note: Low; it is oxidised like black tea, which is why it is not a zero.

name: Licorice tea
description: Licorice root steeped sweet — soothing to the throat, and not for high blood pressure.

tcm.note: Gan cao is neutral and harmonises; it appears in more Chinese formulas than any other herb.

ayurveda.note: Yashtimadhu is shita and madhura — a classical throat and gut soother.

unani.note: Sus is barid-ratab in Unani, a standard demulcent.

histamine.note: Very low. Licorice raises blood pressure with regular use, which is a real caution unrelated to histamine.

nutrition.highlight: in more formulas than any herb

name: Corn silk tea
description: The silk threads from a corn cob, dried and brewed as a diuretic tea.

tcm.note: Yu mi xu is cool and drains damp — a standard drink for water retention.

ayurveda.note: Shita and mutrala.

histamine.note: Very low.

name: Date seed coffee
description: Roasted ground date stones brewed like coffee — caffeine-free, faintly bitter.

tcm.note: Roasted and bitter; no classical entry.

ayurveda.note: Ushna by roasting.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; a Gulf substitute for coffee.

histamine.note: Low; no caffeine, so none of coffee's liberator problem.

name: Mango lassi
description: Yogurt blended with mango pulp and sugar — thick, sweet and everywhere on a curry-house menu.

tcm.note: Yogurt and mango, blended cold.

ayurveda.note: Both dahi and ripe mango are ushna in the classical reading — this is a heating drink, whatever its temperature.

unani.note: Aam is garam; the dahi is thanda, so desi readings split on it.

histamine.note: Low, though it is yogurt plus fruit and does not keep.

name: Salted lassi
description: Yogurt thinned with water, salted and spiked with roasted cumin.

tcm.note: Thinned yogurt, drunk cold.

ayurveda.note: Takra is ushna classically, though the drink is used to cool.

unani.note: Thanda-tar; the standard answer to a hot afternoon and a heavy plate.

histamine.note: Low.

nutrition.highlight: the answer to a hot afternoon

name: Panakam
description: Jaggery water with lemon, ginger and cardamom — offered at Rama Navami, drunk all summer.

tcm.note: Jaggery water with citrus; cooling despite the ginger.

ayurveda.note: Gur and ginger are ushna, lemon more so — heating by the classical reading.

unani.note: Thanda in practice; a temple offering made for the hot season.

histamine.note: Lemon-based, so the citrus flag applies.

nutrition.highlight: a temple offering, and a cooler

name: Coconut malai water
description: Young coconut water drunk with the soft jelly flesh scooped out after.

tcm.note: Read with coconut water, which is cool and generates fluids.

ayurveda.note: Shita; the classical rehydrating drink of the hot months.

histamine.note: Very low — one of the safest drinks on a reactive day.

name: Kvass
description: Fermented rye bread drink — faintly alcoholic, sour and yeasty.

tcm.note: Read with the fermented grain drinks.

ayurveda.note: Fermented and sour, so ushna.

histamine.note: A yeast ferment with residual alcohol — the same combination as beer, and the same problem.

name: Espresso
description: Coffee forced through fine grounds under pressure — concentrated, not just strong.

tcm.note: Read with coffee; concentration intensifies it.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna.

histamine.note: Coffee is a liberator; concentration does not help.

name: Cappuccino
description: Espresso with steamed milk and a deep cap of foam.

tcm.note: Coffee over milk; the coffee dominates.

ayurveda.note: Ushna; milk's shita does not offset it.

histamine.note: Coffee liberator.

name: Cold brew
description: Coffee steeped in cold water for half a day — less acidic, more caffeinated.

tcm.note: Read with coffee; served cold but warming in nature.

ayurveda.note: Ushna.

histamine.note: Coffee liberator; the twelve-hour steep is a long time at room temperature.

name: Instant coffee
description: Brewed coffee dried to granules that dissolve — the household default in much of the world.

tcm.note: Read with coffee.

ayurveda.note: Ushna.

histamine.note: Coffee liberator.

name: Decaf coffee
description: Coffee with the caffeine stripped out — around 97% of it, not all.

tcm.note: Read with coffee; the nature is not in the caffeine.

ayurveda.note: Ushna, if less tikshna.

histamine.note: Still a liberator — the mechanism is not caffeine, which is why decaf disappoints people who switched for that reason.

name: Bubble tea
description: Sweet milk tea with chewy tapioca pearls sitting in the bottom.

tcm.note: Black tea with milk and sugar.

ayurveda.note: Ushna; the tea and sugar over a milk base.

histamine.note: Black tea and non-dairy creamer; the pearls themselves are inert starch.

name: Soda water
description: Water with carbon dioxide dissolved into it, and nothing else.

tcm.note: Plain carbonated water; no classical entry.

ayurveda.note: Shita; essentially water.

histamine.note: None — one of very few drinks that is genuinely nothing.

name: Tonic water
description: Carbonated water with quinine and sugar — bitter, and originally an antimalarial.

tcm.note: Bitter and cooling; no classical entry.

ayurveda.note: Tikta rasa is shita.

histamine.note: Low. Quinine is a real drug at dose, which is a separate caution.

name: Ginger ale
description: Sweet carbonated ginger drink — usually flavouring rather than real ginger.

tcm.note: Ginger-flavoured; warming in nature if it contains real ginger.

ayurveda.note: Ushna, following ginger.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Lemon-lime soda
description: Clear sweet carbonated citrus drink — the one handed over for an upset stomach.

tcm.note: Citrus-flavoured and cold.

ayurveda.note: Sour and ushna, however cold it is served.

histamine.note: Citric acid based.

nutrition.highlight: handed over for a bad stomach

name: Iced tea
description: Black tea brewed strong, sweetened and chilled, usually with lemon.

tcm.note: Black tea served cold with citrus.

ayurveda.note: Tea and lemon are both ushna.

histamine.note: Black tea plus lemon, and bottled versions sit for months.

name: Vimto
description: Dark fruit cordial diluted with water — a Gulf Ramadan fixture despite being British.

tcm.note: A modern cordial; no classical entry.

ayurveda.note: No classical record.

unani.note: Thanda in practice; drunk at iftar.

histamine.note: Concentrated fruit and citric acid.

name: Aloe vera juice
description: The inner leaf gel blended into a slippery, faintly bitter drink.

tcm.note: Lu hui is cold and purgative — a strong classical drug at dose.

ayurveda.note: Kumari is shita and pitta-pacifying, and a classical rasayana for women.

unani.note: Sabr is barid in Unani; used for the liver and for heat.

histamine.note: Low. The latex just under the skin is a strong laxative — a dose matter, not a histamine one.

name: Carrot juice
description: Pressed carrots — sweet, thick and deeply orange.

tcm.note: Read with carrot, which is neutral and moistening.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and madhura in the classical reading.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Beetroot juice
description: Deep red pressed beetroot, earthy and very sweet.

tcm.note: Read with beetroot.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and building; a blood-building juice in desi usage.

histamine.note: Low, though beetroot is high in oxalate and nitrate — separate matters.

name: Green juice
description: Leafy greens, cucumber and apple pressed together — bitter unless there is a lot of apple.

tcm.note: Raw leafy greens, pressed and drunk cold.

ayurveda.note: Shita throughout; strongly pitta-pacifying.

histamine.note: Usually spinach- or chard-based, which is what rates it — the greens, not the process.

name: Watermelon juice
description: Pressed watermelon with nothing added — barely thicker than water.

tcm.note: Read with watermelon, which is cold and clears summer heat.

ayurveda.note: Shita; the classic summer thirst-quencher.

histamine.note: Watermelon carries a mild liberator flag.

name: Guava juice
description: Thick pink guava nectar, usually sold sweetened.

tcm.note: Read with guava.

ayurveda.note: Shita and astringent.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Chai latte
description: Spiced tea concentrate with steamed milk — sweeter and milder than masala chai.

tcm.note: Tea and warm spice over milk.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the tea and masala.

histamine.note: Black tea base, usually from a stored syrup concentrate.

name: Turmeric latte
description: Turmeric, pepper and warm spice whisked into hot milk — haldi doodh, renamed.

tcm.note: Turmeric and pepper over milk.

ayurveda.note: Haridra is ushna and tikshna.

unani.note: Garam-khushk; the classical bedtime drink for cold and cough.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Water kefir
description: Sugar water fermented with kefir grains into a light fizzy drink — no dairy involved.

tcm.note: A ferment on sugar water; no classical entry.

ayurveda.note: Fermented, so ushna.

histamine.note: A live ferment — the same problem as milk kefir and kombucha, without the dairy.

nutrition.highlight: no dairy in it at all

name: Grape juice
description: Pressed grapes, usually the dark sweet kind — unfermented, unlike its famous relative.

tcm.note: Read with grapes, which are neutral and fluid-generating.

ayurveda.note: Draksha is shita and one of the classical sweet fruits.

unani.note: Thanda-tar; angoor is cooling in the Unani record.

histamine.note: Grapes carry more amines than most fruit, which is why wine is so bad — juice is far lower, but not zero.

name: Cranberry juice
description: Tart red juice, almost always sweetened because it is undrinkable otherwise.

tcm.note: A new-world fruit; no classical entry.

ayurveda.note: No classical record.

histamine.note: Very sour.

name: Horchata
description: Tiger nuts or rice steeped, pressed and sweetened with cinnamon — Valencia by way of Al-Andalus.

tcm.note: A cold grain-and-nut milk.

ayurveda.note: Shita; a summer drink.

unani.note: Thanda-tar; the Andalusian summer drink, and Arab in origin.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Sencha
description: The everyday steamed green tea — grassy, and drunk all day.

tcm.note: Green tea is cool and clears heat in the Chinese reading.

ayurveda.note: Shita, though caffeinated.

histamine.note: Low, as green tea is.

name: Hojicha
description: Green tea roasted brown — nutty, low in caffeine, and given to children at night.

tcm.note: Roasting turns a cool tea neutral, which is why it is an evening drink.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; roasting is ushna; the leaf beneath is shita.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; roasted, so drying.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Genmaicha
description: Green tea blended with roasted brown rice, some of it popped.

tcm.note: Green tea with roasted grain — cooler than hojicha, warmer than sencha.

ayurveda.note: Shita, tempered by the roasted rice.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Amazake
description: Rice fermented with koji into a thick sweet drink — sweet without any sugar added.

tcm.note: A warm fermented grain drink.

ayurveda.note: Fermented, so ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; garam by ferment.

histamine.note: A koji ferment — the same mould family as miso, and drunk uncooked.

nutrition.highlight: sweet with no sugar in it

name: Umeshu
description: Green ume steeped in spirit and sugar for months — sweet, sour and strong.

tcm.note: Read with the fruit liqueurs; alcohol is warming.

ayurveda.note: Madya is ushna in a high degree.

histamine.note: Alcohol plus months of steeping on sour fruit — both mechanisms.

name: Shochu
description: Distilled from barley, sweet potato or rice — lighter than whisky, stronger than sake.

tcm.note: Distilled liquor is the hottest drink in the Chinese materia.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna in the highest degree of the madya group.

histamine.note: Distilling leaves most histamine behind, but the alcohol still blocks DAO.

name: Makgeolli
description: Cloudy unfiltered rice brew, lightly fizzy and only mildly alcoholic.

tcm.note: A warm fermented grain drink.

ayurveda.note: Madya is ushna.

histamine.note: Unfiltered and still fermenting in the bottle — live yeast plus alcohol.

name: Soju
description: Clear neutral spirit, distilled or diluted — the default Korean drink.

tcm.note: Distilled liquor is the hottest drink in the Chinese materia.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and tikshna in the highest degree of madya.

histamine.note: Distilled, so lower in histamine than beer or wine — but the alcohol still blocks DAO.

name: Sikhye
description: Sweet cloudy rice drink made with malt — served ice cold after a meal.

tcm.note: Served cold; malted rice, lightly sweet.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; read with the sweet grain drinks.

histamine.note: Malt-fermented, though only briefly and then cooked.

nutrition.highlight: served ice cold, after a meal

name: Yuja cha
description: Sliced citron preserved in honey and stirred into hot water.

tcm.note: Aromatic citrus peel with honey — warming.

ayurveda.note: Madhu is ushna.

histamine.note: Citrus peel preserved in sugar for months.

name: Omija tea
description: Schisandra berries steeped cold — sour, sweet, bitter, salty and pungent at once.

tcm.note: Wu wei zi is warm and astringent, a classical lung and kidney tonic.

ayurveda.note: Outside the classical record; sour and astringent; read as ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; placed with the astringent tonics.

histamine.note: Sour berry infusion.

name: Maesil cha
description: Green plums steeped in sugar for months, then diluted hot or cold.

tcm.note: Sour fruit syrup, usually drunk cold.

ayurveda.note: Amla-rasa and ushna.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; thanda in practice; taken for digestion.

histamine.note: Months of sugar-steeping on sour fruit.

name: Insam cha
description: Ginseng root steeped or powdered into a bitter-sweet tonic tea.

tcm.note: Ren shen is warm and the archetypal qi tonic — held back in heat conditions.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and building.

histamine.note: Low.

name: Daechu cha
description: Red dates simmered long and sweetened — thick, dark and warming.

tcm.note: Da zao is warm and tonifies qi and blood.

ayurveda.note: Ushna and building.

unani.note: Outside the classical record; garam-tar; a winter tonic.

histamine.note: Dried fruit, long-simmered.

name: Misugaru
description: Mixed roasted grains and beans ground to powder and shaken into milk or water.

tcm.note: Roasted grains; warming and drying.

ayurveda.note: Ushna from the roasting.

histamine.note: Low.
